status: All 51 Linux attempts passed; all 87 scheduled attempts, including the separate 36 finite-work trials, passed without retries.

scope.primary_interval: Immediately before QEMU spawn through receipt of the full common pre-request serial token, including startup, QMP setup and stock Linux boot.
scope.guest: Identical frozen stock Linux 7.2.3 kernel and shared serial initramfs, with unchanged production CPU, machine, RTC and seed settings. No guest boot shaping or kernel fast-boot options.
scope.direct_cumulative_result: Seven literal-origin/final complete pairs on the same new guest. The cumulative result is measured directly, not assembled by adding stage or microbenchmark percentages.
scope.normal_contracts: Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG at one nanosecond per retired instruction, and Sim at 50 picoseconds per retired instruction with authenticated scheduler control have different clock and control contracts.
scope.native_sim: All 18 witness fields are exact across all 25 final-campaign Sim samples and retained same-guest references. The authenticated sequence-two stop is request raw plus one and logical tick plus 50, with native paused acknowledgement.
scope.capture: All declared 256 MiB RAM, registers, markers, actual grants and completed timer witness are captured outside primary timing. The stopped semantic tuple is rechecked after RAM capture.
scope.ordinary_counts: Post-marker QMP stop and replay counts are late diagnostics, not exact serial-token instruction coordinates. No-icount zero counts are not a guest-work measurement.
scope.cpu_accounting: Sim CPU counters end after native paused acknowledgement; ordinary counters end shortly after serial receipt. Neither is an exact CPU counter coordinate at the common marker.
scope.device_projection: Device projection manifests validate schema only; they are not fingerprints of every modeled device value.
scope.balance: Normal five-row/five-round trials cover each position once in one forward cycle. Odd-count paired campaigns alternate order but give the first label one extra first position.
scope.statistics: All natural variation is retained. No uncertainty bound or general workload speed claim is inferred from these local samples.

timing_window.scope: Root-coordinated team quiet window, with no Firecracker observed by the parent at the start. Whole-host idleness is not established.
timing_window.per_trial_utc: The frozen runners did not record individual trial UTC endpoints. Stored durations and ordering are exact; file modification times are not substituted as timing endpoints.

raw_results.scope:
Compare ordinary TCG and Sim through the same complete serial milestone.

All rows boot identical stock kernel and initramfs bytes. The primary interval
starts before QEMU spawn and ends when the common socket reader receives the
complete pre-request token. It includes emulator startup, QMP setup and boot;
protocol allocation and post-marker diagnostics are outside the interval.

Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG with 1 ns per instruction, and Sim
with 50 ps per instruction use different execution contracts. Their same-workload
boot latency comparison is not a measurement of equal-instruction overhead.
Sim's authenticated native stop, full RAM, registers and timer witness are
qualified separately after the common marker. Stock post-marker QMP stops are
not exact token coordinates. CPU accounting endpoints are recorded per row.

Build the new guest and driver with the AOS phase2.tcgLinuxSerialGuest and

row explicitly as --row LABEL MODE QEMU_BINARY PLUGIN_OR_DASH. Modes are tcg,

in ordinary TCG rows, even when the emulator supports them. Repeated rounds
rotate row positions and then reverse the rotations. Every start, exit, stream,
raw result and failed attempt is retained; no failed trial is retried or replaced.

raw_results.scope:
Compare ordinary TCG and Sim through the same complete serial milestone.

All rows boot identical stock kernel and initramfs bytes. The primary interval
starts before QEMU spawn and ends when the common socket reader receives the
complete pre-request token. It includes emulator startup, QMP setup and boot;
protocol allocation and post-marker diagnostics are outside the interval.

Ordinary TCG without icount, ordinary TCG with 1 ns per instruction, and Sim
with 50 ps per instruction use different execution contracts. Their same-workload
boot latency comparison is not a measurement of equal-instruction overhead.
Sim's authenticated native stop, full RAM, registers and timer witness are
qualified separately after the common marker. Stock post-marker QMP stops are
not exact token coordinates. CPU accounting endpoints are recorded per row.

Build the new guest and driver with the AOS phase2.tcgLinuxSerialGuest and
phase2.tcgLinuxSerialPerformanceDriver targets using local builders. Pass each
row explicitly as --row LABEL MODE QEMU_BINARY PLUGIN_OR_DASH. Modes are tcg,
tcg-icount and sim; ordinary TCG takes '-' for the plugin. No plugins are loaded
in ordinary TCG rows, even when the emulator supports them. Repeated rounds
rotate row positions and then reverse the rotations. Every start, exit, stream,
raw result and failed attempt is retained; no failed trial is retried or replaced.
